text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) is diagnosed when readings consistently measure 130/80 mm Hg or higher.
Blood pressure is recorded as two numbers:

list.snippet: Systolic (top number): Pressure when the heart beats.
Diastolic (bottom number): Pressure when the heart rests between beats.

text_blocks.snippet: According to the American Heart Association guidelines, adult blood pressure falls into these ranges:

list.snippet: Elevated: Systolic 120–129 and diastolic less than 80 mm Hg
Stage 1 Hypertension: Systolic 130–139 or diastolic 80–89 mm Hg
Stage 2 Hypertension: Systolic 140 mm Hg or higher or diastolic 90 mm Hg or higher
Hypertensive Crisis: Systolic higher than 180 and/or diastolic higher than 120 mm Hg (requires immediate medical attention)
